headline: Chip-assembly equipment maker Besi has joined Applied Materials' research centre as an innovation partner to work on chip-stacking for AI.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: official partnership news, but a research collaboration with no products or dates.
importance_line: It affects chip designers who need denser stacking for AI hardware, but it is a research partnership announced by the companies themselves, with no products, results or timelines.
summary: Applied Materials and BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) announced, as carried by DQ, that they are expanding their partnership begun in 2020, with Besi joining Applied's EPIC Center in Silicon Valley as an Innovation Partner to co-develop packaging steps such as hybrid bonding, a way of joining stacked chips directly, and panel-level integration. The companies say the aim is to give shared customers earlier access to co-optimised processes for AI chips; the announcement gives no results or product dates.
notes: DQ India carries the companies' own announcement (quotes Gary Dickerson, Richard Blickman and Prabu Raja), so the companies are credited. Date of the announcement is not stated in the text; published 9 Oct. The $5 billion EPIC figure and 'largest-ever US investment' are the companies' claim.
